newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to nationalise two local government banks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to nationalise two local government banks.

text.p: Taiwan's Finance Minister Paul Chiu plans to nationalise two Taiwan Provincial Government-run banks within six months, officials said on Friday.

A finance ministry official said a parliamentary joint committee on Thursday decided to seek nationalisation of the Bank of Taiwan and Land Bank of Taiwan. The official said Chiu expected negotiations with the provincial government to take six months .
Bank of Taiwan is the island's largest commercial bank.
The official quoted Chiu as saying the central government owns 100 percent of the two banks' initial capitalisation. It commissioned the provincial government to run the banks in 1946.
The move would lift state treasury annual income by about T$20 billion -- some T$15 billion from the Bank of Taiwan and some T$4-5 billion from Land Bank, the official said.

The local Economic Daily News on Friday reported that the provincial government strongly objected to the ministry's plan, quoting provincial governor James Soong as saying: "They (the two banks) are owned by the provincial government."
The paper said Bank of Taiwan had reinvested in other provincial government-owned banks whose total values now were more than T$300 billion.
Bank of Taiwan owns 49.12 percent of Hua Nan Bank, 12.84 percent of First Bank and 0.23 percent of Chang Hwa Bank, the paper said.
The provincial government runs most of the island country except Taipei and Kaohsiung.
